title: Watercolor
text:
The golden shacks fenced with thistles;

pigs in the streets;

a cartwheel

beside a shack, a latrine in the yard,

a girl filling her jar,

and Momotombo

blue, behind the cheerful underwear hanging up

yellow, white, pink.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the watercolor-like inventory of rural detail with Momotombo behind the laundry.

title: In Losing You, You and I Have Lost...
text:
In losing you, you and I have lost:

I, because you were what I loved most,

and you, because I was the one who loved you most.


But of the two of us, you lose more than I do:

because I will be able to love others as I loved you,

but you will not be loved as I loved you.
editorial_note: The translation follows the poem's measured argument about unequal loss after separation.

title: I Still Remember
text:
I still remember

that street

of yellow lamps,

with that full

moon among the electric

wires


And that star

on the corner,

a distant radio,

the tower of La Merced

that struck those

eleven:


And the golden light

of your open

door, on that street.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the remembered street as a sequence of lamps, wires, bells, and the beloved's doorway.

title: Our Relationship
text:
Our relationship...

This symbiosis that we are.

You know what I was looking for:

beauty that does not grow fat,

love that does not become bourgeois.

On the other hand you:

wanted to have love with someone

for what I was made.

I did nothing to make you fall in love.

My renunciations

are still dripping blood.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the uneasy intimacy, anti-bourgeois desire, and the bleeding cost of renunciation.

title: Time, I Hate You. Though Without You I Would Not Exist
text:
Time, I hate you. Though without you I would not exist.

And by your passing I will die though by your passing I was born.

Like Saint Francis Borgia I now want

to love someone whom time does not touch

and for us to rent a room where night does not pass

nor the neon signs go out one by one.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradox of hating time while owing birth to it, ending in a room outside night.
